humanRulings.decision:
Ability modifier:

`floor((abilityScore - 10) / 2)`

Rules:

- Use mathematical floor.
- Ability scores must be positive integers.
- Do not impose a generic maximum score of 20.
- Explicit feature-specific maximums or minimums take precedence.
- Species modifiers are applied according to existing character-creation rules.
- The engine must support legitimate scores above 20.

Update calculation policies, validation and tests.

Mark PHB-RULE-009 RESOLVED.

## Default Weapon Ability Binding

Normal melee weapon:

- Attack ability: Strength
- Damage ability: Strength

Normal ranged weapon:

- Attack ability: Dexterity
- Damage ability: Dexterity

Finesse:

- Strength or Dexterity
- The same selected ability is used for attack and damage

Thrown:

- Uses the ability the weapon would normally use for its melee attack unless an explicit rule overrides it

Spirit Weapon:

- May substitute the user's psychic ability for Strength/Dexterity for attack and damage

Explicit weapon-specific rules override all defaults.

## Save-Based Weapons

Save-based weapon effects do not automatically add an ability modifier to their listed damage.

Only add an ability modifier when a rule explicitly says to do so.

Grenades and similar fixed-damage save effects therefore use their listed damage dice.

## Hands

Defaults:

- Pistol: 1
- Light melee weapon: 1
- Shield: 1
- Normal melee weapon: 1
- Heavy melee weapon: 2
- Versatile: 1 or 2
- Basic firearm: 2
- Shotgun: 2
- Sniper weapon: 2
- Heavy ranged weapon: 2

Add explicit overrides where required.

Force Staff is explicitly 2-handed.

## Reach

- Default melee reach: 5 ft
- Ranged weapons have no melee reach unless a rule gives them one
- Thrown melee weapons retain normal melee reach as well as their throwing range

## Proficiency Groups

Canonical weapon entities must have explicit `proficiencyGroups`.

Support groups including at minimum:

- simple_melee
- martial_melee
- pistol
- basic_firearm
- shotgun
- sniper
- heavy
- grenade
- flamer
- chain
- shock
- plasma
- melta
- force
- shield
- ogryn
- kin
- aeldari
- mechanicus
- rad_weapon
- advanced_firearm
- improvised
- mining_tool

Weapons may belong to more than one group.

Properties may help derive initial group membership, but canonical records must store membership explicitly.

## Starting Equipment Proficiency

A class is proficient with every weapon or shield granted directly by its own level-1 starting-equipment package.

For a package choice, this applies to the selected option.

Do not use this rule to grant unrelated weapon-group proficiency.

## Emplaced Weapons

Emplaced is a deployment restriction, not a proficiency.

Represent conceptually as:

- deployment: emplaced
- requires mount, brace, rig, feature or GM-approved setup

Do not create an `emplaced proficiency`.

Mark PHB-RULE-024 RESOLVED.

`medkit` in starting equipment is an alias for the canonical Med-Pack.

Do not create a separate Medkit entity.

Update all starting-package references to use the canonical Med-Pack entity while retaining "medkit" as a recognised display/source alias if useful.

Mark PHB-RULE-049 RESOLVED.

Riot Shield uses the generic Shield profile:

- +2 AC
- requires one hand

Add appropriate tags such as:

- shield
- riot
- arbites

It qualifies for features that require or reference using a shield.

Do not duplicate the full Shield rules in a separate incompatible entity.

Mark PHB-RULE-050 RESOLVED.

## Generic Starting Light Armour Pool

The starting-equipment option `light armour` contains:

- Armoured Bodyglove
- Mesh Armour

Do not include:

- Heavy Clothing
- Flak armour
- Species-pattern armour

Heavy Clothing remains a separately selectable item where explicitly offered.

## Minor Augmetic Pool

`minor augmetic` means a Controlled-Availability Augmetic Upgrade.

The current approved pool is:

- Optical Implant
- Respirator Implant
- Data-Jack
- Vox Implant
- Mag-Lock Palm
- Dermal Insulation
- Internal Chrono
- Mechadendrite, Utility
- Black-Iron Jaw
- Vocal Coder

Scarce and Rare augmetics do not belong to the generic Minor Augmetic pool.

## Narrative / Utility Starting Items

Canonicalise the following without inventing automatic mechanical bonuses:

- Symbol of Faith: narrative item
- Sanctioning brands/restraints: narrative item
- Psychic Focus: tagged functional item `psychic_focus`, no inherent numerical bonus
- Rations: general/narrative supply
- Lucky Charm: narrative trinket
- Manacles: utility/manual adjudication
- Black-market contact: character contact, not inventory
- Camo cloak: equipment; manual effect until explicitly defined
- Maintenance tools: utility/tool item
- Oath-token: narrative item; does not grant Relic-Bearer
- Survey auspex: scanner/auspex variant with manual utility
- Climbing kit: utility/tool item
- Claim marker: narrative/feature prop
- Spirit-token: narrative item
- Rune stones: Psychic Focus variant
- Spirit charm: narrative item

A canonical inventory item may legitimately have no automated combat mechanics.

Mark PHB-RULE-051 RESOLVED.

humanRulings.decision:
# Approved PHB-RULE-007 — Rare / Limited Origin Availability

Origin availability uses three production-relevant states.

## NORMAL

The Species/Origin combination is legal without additional approval, assuming all other prerequisites are satisfied.

## RARE

The Species/Origin combination is a legal player option but requires explicit GM approval.

Rare does NOT mean:

- invalid
- NPC-only
- automatically selectable

Until the application has a trusted GM/campaign approval mechanism, Rare combinations may be displayed but must not be available for ordinary self-service character creation.

## LIMITED

The Species/Origin combination is an exceptional player option.

It requires explicit GM/campaign approval for the specific combination and appropriate narrative justification.

Limited approval must be specific to the affected Species/Origin combination.

A generic `allow rare content` permission is not sufficient for Limited options.

Until a trusted campaign approval mechanism exists, Limited combinations may be displayed but must remain unavailable for ordinary self-service character creation.

Represent these states structurally.

Do not hard-code approval behaviour into React.

Mark PHB-RULE-007 RESOLVED.

itemRulings.decision:
For the canonical Frag Grenade:

## Failed Dexterity Save

Take:

`3d6 piercing damage`

## Successful Dexterity Save

Take:

`half of the rolled 3d6 piercing damage, rounded down`

## Ability Modifier

Do not add an ability modifier to Frag Grenade damage.

## Area

15-ft radius.

## Save

Use the existing canonical grenade save DC policy.

## Consumption

The grenade remains expended after use according to the existing grenade rules.

This ruling is specific to the Frag Grenade profile.

It does NOT establish a generic rule that:

- all Blast effects deal half damage on success
- all area weapons deal half damage on success
- all grenades deal half damage on success

Other unresolved Blast/save effects must retain their current blocked state unless their own source text explicitly defines the result.

di.background.craftworld_outcast.descriptionMarkdown:
4.9 Craftworld / Outcast
Raised among Aeldari ways, then sent away, exiled, self-
exiled, ranger-bound, corsair-adjacent, or
drawn into a dangerous path beyond normal craftworld 
protection.
Allowed Species: Aeldari.
Skill Proficiency: Choose two from Acrobatics, Insight, 
Perception, Stealth, Survival, and Technology.
Path Discipline: Once per long rest, when you fail a 
Wisdom or Intelligence saving throw, you may
reroll it. You must use the new result.
Alien Poise: You have advantage on checks to move 
silently through ruins, forests, webway structures,
wraithbone architecture, or abandoned alien sites.

4.5 Forge World
Raised among manufactorums, machine temples, data-
vaults, and sacred industry.
Allowed Species: Human, Skitarii.
Skill Proficiency: Investigation and Technology.

power systems.

advantage on a saving throw against fear, panic, or
psychic manipulation.

di.background.hiveborn.descriptionMarkdown:
4.1 Hiveborn
Raised in the brutal density of a hive city.
Allowed Species: Human, Ratling, rare Ogryn.
Skill Proficiency: Choose one from Deception, Insight, 
Intimidation, Sleight of Hand, or Stealth.
Crowd Rat: You ignore difficult terrain caused by 
crowds, rubble, cramped spaces, pipes, gantries, and
dense urban clutter.
Seen Worse: You have advantage on saving throws 
against fear caused by gore, violence, intimidation,
or battlefield horror.

di.background.militarum_regiment.descriptionMarkdown:
4.7 Militarum Regiment
Formerly attached to an Imperial Guard force, auxiliary 
formation, or battlefield logistics unit.
Allowed Species: Human, Ogryn, Ratling, limited 
Skitarii.
Skill Proficiency: Choose one from Athletics or Survival, 
and gain Perception.
Squad Drill: Before initiative is rolled, choose one ally 
within 5 ft of you who can see or hear you. You
and that chosen ally each gain +1 to initiative for that 
combat. You must choose the ally before anyone
rolls initiative. If no ally is within 5 ft when initiative is 
called, this feature provides no benefit.
Field Discipline: Once per short rest, you may reroll a 
failed saving throw against Suppression.

Raised in a Squat/Kin hold, mining fleet, oath-band, 
salvage guild, prospecting clan, or void-industrial

the new result.

di.background.penal_worlder.descriptionMarkdown:
4.3 Penal Worlder
A convict, survivor, conscript, or former prisoner.
Allowed Species: Human, Ogryn, Ratling.
Skill Proficiency: Survival and one of Athletics, 
Deception, or Intimidation.
Hard Time: You have advantage on saving throws 
against exhaustion caused by forced marches,
starvation, poor conditions, or sleep deprivation.
Dirty Survival: Once per long rest, when you are 
reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you
may drop to 1 hit point instead.

di.background.shrine_worlder.descriptionMarkdown:
4.2 Shrine Worlder
Raised in devotion, ritual, sacrifice, and Imperial worship.
Allowed Species: Human, rare Ratling.
Skill Proficiency: Religion and either Persuasion or 
Intimidation.
Litany of Resolve: Once per long rest, you can give 
yourself or one ally within 30 ft. advantage on a Wisdom 
saving throw.
Sacred Hatred: Once per turn, when you damage a 
heretic, daemon, mutant, witch, traitor, or xenos with
a weapon attack or class feature, you deal an additional 
1d4 + 1 radiant damage.
This damage represents zeal, ritual fury, and trained 
hatred rather than true divine magic.

Raised below the proper world, among gangs, sump-rats, 
chem dens, scavvers, and forgotten habs.
Allowed Species: Human, Ratling.
Skill Proficiency: Choose two from Deception, 
Intimidation, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, and Survival.
Black-Market Instinct: You know how to locate illegal 
goods, smugglers, fences, and information
brokers in hive settlements.
Never Fight Fair: Once per short rest, when you hit a 
creature that has not acted yet in combat, deal
additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

vessel, or ancient wreck.
Allowed Species: Human, Ratling, rare Ogryn.

manualRules.text:
11.12 Aeldari Warlock
An Aeldari battle-seer, a former Seer who has walked the Path of the Warrior, or rune-armoured psyker
operating under a hidden command. This is not a normal Imperial psyker and should be used carefully.
Allowed Species: Aeldari only.
Hit Die: d6.
Primary Abilities: Wisdom or Intelligence, Dexterity.
Saving Throws: Wisdom, Intelligence.
Armour: Aeldari mesh, rune armour.
Weapons: Aeldari weapons, witchblades, singing spears, pistols.
Special: Uses Runes of Battle and Warp Pressure. Aeldari Warlocks do not learn Malefic powers.

manualRules.text:
Blank / Null-Bound is a GM-permission discipline. It 
represents a sanctioned blank, null-scarred operative, or 
anti-psyker weapon rather than a conventional Warp-
channelling psyker.
Blank / Null-Bound characters may learn Universal and 
Null powers, cannot learn Malefic
powers, and should be rare in the same way as Aeldari 
player characters.
When a Psyker chooses a Psychic Discipline, that choice 
determines which non-universal powers they
can learn. A Psyker may always learn Universal powers. 
They may only learn discipline-locked powers
from their chosen discipline unless the GM grants an 
exception through a relic, corruption event,
mentor, sanctioning scar, or major campaign reward.

manualRules.text:
A Psyker has a score called Warp Pressure.
Warp Pressure starts at 0.
Whenever you use a psychic power, increase your Warp 
Pressure by that power’s cost.
After resolving the power, roll a d20. If the result is equal 
to or lower than your current Warp Pressure,
Perils of the Warp triggers.
Example:
● Your Warp Pressure is 5.
● You cast Focused Rupture.
● Focused Rupture adds +2 Warp Pressure.
● Your Warp Pressure is now 7.
● You roll a d20.
● On a 1- 7, Perils trigger.

wraithbone architecture, or abandoned alien sites.

formation, or battlefield logistics unit.
Allowed Species: Human, Ogryn, Ratling, limited

called, this feature provides no benefit.

failed saving throw against Suppression.

3.6 Aeldari / Eldar
Aeldari are ancient xenos whose reflexes, senses, and 
psychic presence far exceed human norms. Player
Aeldari should represent rare outcasts, rangers, corsair-
adjacent wanderers, or warlocks operating
under a specific hidden purpose.
Size: Medium.

Available Classes: Aeldari Outcast, Aeldari Warlock.
3.6.1 Aeldari Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 90 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Inhuman Grace: Gain proficiency in Acrobatics or 
Stealth.
Keen Senses: Gain proficiency in Perception. If you 
already have Perception proficiency, add +1 to
Perception checks instead.
Battle Trance: You may move through the space of 
allied creatures without treating it as difficult
terrain. Once per short rest, when you move at least 10 ft 
before making a weapon attack, add +1d4 to
the attack roll.
Ancient Mind: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being charmed or frightened by non-psychic 
effects.
Xenos Distrust: You have disadvantage on Persuasion 
checks with most Imperial authorities unless
disguised, vouched for, or operating under an established 
truce.

manualRules.text:
3.5 Squat / Kin
Squats, often known as Kin in modern Imperial records, 
are hardy void-adapted abhumans associated
with holds, guilds, oath-bands, mining fleets, mercenary 
contracts, and ancient grudges. They are
shorter than humans but dense, resilient, technically 
minded, and extremely difficult to intimidate.
Size: Medium, but your height is usually between 4 and 5 
ft.

Available Classes: Kin Armsman, Hernkyn Prospector.
3.5.1 Squat / Kin Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 60 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Dense Build: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being shoved, knocked prone, or moved
against your will.
Void-Hardened: You have advantage on saving throws 
against exhaustion caused by poor atmosphere,
bad rations, forced marches, cramped voidship 
conditions, mining hazards, or environmental hardship.
Guild-Craft: Gain proficiency in Technology, 
Investigation, or one artisan/tool proficiency related to
engineering, mining, weapons, armour, or voidcraft.
Grudge Memory: Once per long rest, when a creature 
damages you or an ally within 30 ft, mark that
creature as the subject of a grudge. The first time you hit 
that creature before the end of the encounter,
add your proficiency bonus to the damage.
Stubborn Kin: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.

manualRules.text:
3.2 Ogryn Abhuman
Ogryns are massive abhumans used by the Imperium as 
shock troops, bodyguards, line-breakers, and
living siege weapons. They are loyal and terrifyingly 
durable, but they are not subtle and struggle with
equipment designed for normal human frames.
Size: Medium, but you count as one size larger for 
carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, and
shoving.

Available Classes: Ogryn Skullbreaker only.
3.2.1 Ogryn Traits
Massive Build: Your maximum hit points increase by 3 
per character level. You also count as one size
larger for carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, 
and shoving.
Thick Skull: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.
Brute Strength: Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 + your 
Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.
Too Big for Standard Kit: You cannot use most 
standard armour, delicate weapons, compact firearms,
or subtle tools unless they have been modified for Ogryn 
use.
Simple Solutions: You are not automatically stupid, but 
you struggle with delicate logic, subtle
interfaces, encrypted systems, and advanced technology. 
You have disadvantage on Intelligence checks
involving advanced technology, forbidden lore, cogitators, 
security systems, encrypted data, or complex
machinery unless you are proficient in a relevant skill or 
tool. However, once per short rest, when a
problem could plausibly be solved through brute force, 
intimidation, endurance, or direct action, you
may add your proficiency bonus to the check even if you 
would not normally be proficient.

3.3 Ratling Abhuman
Ratlings are small abhumans known for stealth, 
marksmanship, scavenging, cooking, black-market
dealings, and improbable survival.
Size: Small.

Available Classes: Ratling Sharpshooter, Veteran, Hive 
Scum.
3.3.1 Ratling Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 60 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Small Target: When you have light cover, you may treat 
it as heavy cover.
Sniper’s Eye: You ignore disadvantage from attacking at 
long range with weapons that have the
Accurate property.
Lucky Shot: Once per short rest, when you miss with a 
ranged weapon attack, you may reroll the
attack.
Bad in a Straight Fight: You have disadvantage on 
Strength checks made to shove or grapple creatures
larger than you.

3.4 Skitarii Augmented Human
Skitarii are cybernetically enhanced soldiers of the 
Adeptus Mechanicus. They are machine-disciplined,
sensor-linked, and doctrinally conditioned beyond normal 
human limits.
Size: Medium.

Available Classes: Skitarii Veteran.
3.4.1 Skitarii Traits
Augmetic Body: You have resistance to poison damage 
and advantage on saving throws against
disease.
Machine Discipline: You have advantage on saving 
throws against being charmed.
Noospheric Focus: Gain proficiency in Investigation, 
Perception, or Technology.
Integrated Auspex: Once per short rest, as a bonus 
action, choose one creature within 60 ft that you
can see. Your next attack against that creature before 
the end of your turn gains +1d4 to hit.
Cybernetic Maintenance: During a short rest, if you or 
an ally has tinker’s tools or Mechanicus tools,
you may regain additional hit points equal to your 
proficiency bonus.
No Psychic Potential: You cannot choose the Psyker 
class or any trait that grants psychic powers.

manualRules.text:
Revised cost table
Each psychic power increases Warp Pressure. Empowering a power now concretely changes the power
and increases risk.
Power Type Warp Pressure Cost
Minor Power +1 Warp Pressure
Standard Power +2 Warp Pressure
Major Power +3 Warp Pressure
Empowered Power +1 additional Warp Pressure, plus one Empowered effect below
Empowered Option Effect
Overcharged Damage If the power deals damage, add one additional damage die of the 
same type.
Brutal Manifestation If the power requires a saving throw, increase the Psychic Save 
DC by +1 for that casting.
Extended Reach Increase the range by 30 ft, or increase a cone/area radius by 5 ft.
Sustained Focus If the power grants temporary hit points, healing, protection, or a 
bonus, increase the value by your proficiency bonus.
Split Manifestation If the power targets one creature and does not already affect 
multiple targets, target one additional creature within 10 ft of the 
original target. The second target takes half damage or receives 
half the non-damage effect, GM adjudication.
Discipline Mastery If the power belongs to your chosen discipline, you may reroll one 
damage die or healing die from the power.
Empowered restriction
A power can only be Empowered once per casting. Empowering a power always increases Warp Pressure
before the Perils roll is made. Minor powers can be empowered, but doing so is reckless and should feel
dangerous at low levels.

Power Tag Rule
Warp Spark Universal Action. Range 60 ft. Psychic attack. On hit, 1d8 force damage.
Kinetic Push Telekinesis, Universal Action. Range 30 ft. Strength save. Failure: pushed 10 ft and takes 1d6 force damage.
Mind Lumen Divination, Universal Bonus Action. Self. 10 minutes. See psychic traces, Warp residue, emotional 
impressions, and unnatural disturbances within 30 ft.
Static Veil Telekinesis, Universal Reaction. Trigger: targeted by a ranged attack. Add +2 AC against that attack.
Flesh Knit Biomancy Action. Touch. A creature regains 1d6 + psychic ability modifier HP.
Pain Spike Biomancy Action. Range 60 ft. Constitution save. Failure: 1d8 psychic damage, and the target 
cannot take reactions.
Ember Flicker Pyromancy Bonus Action. Range 30 ft. Ignite or extinguish a small flame; one creature takes 1 fire 
damage if holding a flammable object.
Power Tag Rule
Ashen Brand Pyromancy Action. Range: 60 ft. Psychic attack. On hit, 1d8 fire/radiant damage, and the target 
sheds dim light until your next turn.
Danger Sense Divination Reaction. When you roll initiative, add 1d4 to your initiative roll.
Echo Read Divination Action. Touch an object or corpse. Learn one recent strong emotion, danger, or image 
attached to it.
Whisper from Below Malefic Bonus Action. Range 30 ft. One creature makes a Wisdom save. Failure: disadvantage 
on the next Wisdom saving throw before your next turn.
Warp Bite Malefic Action. Range 60 ft. Psychic attack. On hit, 1d10 psychic damage. If you roll a natural 
1, immediately add +1 Warp Pressure.
Null Glare Null Action. Range 30 ft. One creature makes a Charisma save. Failure: it has 
disadvantage on the next psychic attack roll it makes, or the next saving throw it 
forces, before your next turn.
Blank Sense Null Bonus Action. Self. 10 minutes. Sense active psychic effects, daemonic influence, 
blanks, and Warp residue within 30 ft.

A Psyker has a score called Warp Pressure.
Warp Pressure starts at 0.
Whenever you use a psychic power, increase your Warp 
Pressure by that power’s cost.
After resolving the power, roll a d20. If the result is equal 
to or lower than your current Warp Pressure,
Perils of the Warp triggers.
Example:
● Your Warp Pressure is 5.
● You cast Focused Rupture.
● Focused Rupture adds +2 Warp Pressure.
● Your Warp Pressure is now 7.
● You roll a d20.
● On a 1- 7, Perils trigger.

Aeldari Warlocks use the standard Perils rules unless the GM chooses to use this specialised
table. These results should feel like rune backlash, spirit-stone shrieking, fate distortion, or
webway trauma rather than crude daemonic possession.
Severity Aeldari Peril Result
2-6 Rune Static You take 1d6 psychic damage and cannot use Rune Ward until the start of your next turn.
7-10 Ghosthelm Pain You take 2d6 psychic damage and have disadvantage on your next psychic attack roll or psychic 
saving throw before the end of your next turn.
11-14 Ancestral Echo Every creature within 10 ft hears dead voices through your mind. Each creature, including you, 
takes 1d6 psychic damage and cannot take reactions until its next turn.
15-18 Fate Snarl Until the end of your next turn, the first d20 roll made by you or an ally within 30 ft is reduced by 
1d4.
19-22 Spirit-Stone Cry You are incapacitated until the end of your next turn. One ally within 30 ft takes 1d6 psychic 
damage unless they succeed on a Wisdom save against your Psychic Save DC.
23-26 Rune Miscast The GM chooses a Warlock, Divination, or Telekinesis power you know. It immediately targets a 
random valid creature or location.
27-30 Webway Shear A 10-ft radius area within 30 ft becomes distorted terrain for 1 minute. A creature entering it for the 
first time on a turn or starting there takes 2d6 force damage.
31+ Doom of the Seer You drop to 0 hit points. Every creature within 30 ft takes 4d6 psychic damage. You gain 1 
Corruption or a GM-approved Doom Mark tied to Aeldari fate, spirit-stones, or daemonic pursuit.

Perils severity roll. These results should feel predatory, corrupting, and narratively dangerous.
Severity Malefic Peril Result
2-6 Malignant Static You take 1d6 psychic damage and have disadvantage on your next saving throw against fear, 
charm, or corruption.
7-10 Blooded Eyes You take 2d6 psychic damage and a nearby Warp entity, cult icon, or daemon-touched creature 
becomes aware of your presence.
11-14 Predatory Echo Every creature within 10 ft, including you, takes 2d6 psychic damage. The GM may describe a 
hostile voice, omen, or watching presence.
15-18 Daemon Scream Creatures of your choice within 30 ft must make a Wisdom save or become frightened until the 
end of their next turn. After Perils is reduced, your Warp Pressure increases by 1.
19-22 Possession Pressure You are incapacitated until the end of your next turn. Make a Charisma save against your Psychic 
Save DC; on a failure, gain 1 Corruption.
23-26 Unbidden Manifestation The GM chooses a random Malefic power you know. If you know no valid Malefic power, Terror 
Echo manifests instead. The target is random.
27-30 Reality Wound A 10-ft radius area within 30 ft becomes corrupted terrain for 1 minute. Creatures entering or 
starting there take 2d6 psychic damage. Daemons and corrupted creatures have advantage on 
their next attack made from inside it.
31+ Catastrophic Breach You drop to 0 hit points. Every creature within 30 ft takes 4d6 psychic damage. A hostile Warp 
entity, possession threat, or daemon sign enters the scene, and you gain 2 Corruption instead of 
1.

manualRules.text:
Characters can recover enemy equipment, but a battlefield is not a consequence-free catalogue. Salvage bypasses the 
question of whether the item physically exists; it does not bypass condition, ammunition, legality, compatibility, 
ownership or maintenance.
Step Player Procedure
1. Secure
The item must actually be recovered from 
the scene. A retreat, collapsing site or 
hostile reinforcements can make this 
impossible.
2. Assess
Use Investigation, Technology or an 
appropriate tool proficiency when the item's 
condition, traps, corruption or unfamiliar 
technology is uncertain.
3. Restore
Damaged or Worn gear may require parts, a 
maintenance kit, workshop time or a project 
before it can be trusted.
4. Integrate
Unfamiliar, species-pattern, Mechanicus, 
xenos or proscribed gear may require 
training, an interface, ammunition or a 
specialist before use.
5. Explain
If authorities care about ownership or 
legality, the warband needs a believable 
provenance, permit, patron or very 
convincing lie.
Recovering an item therefore does not require a normal Requisition test, but keeping it may create an equivalent cost in 
repairs, contacts, Heat, favours or narrative risk. This is deliberate: loot should create choices rather than convert every 
battlefield into a shopping trip.

Any Near-Unique or Unique item is Signature Wargear. A character may benefit from no more than three Signature 
items at the same time. Additional Signature items may be carried, stored or entrusted to allies, but provide no 
mechanical benefit until exchanged during a long rest or suitable downtime. Rare and Exceptional items do not count 
unless their entry specifically says otherwise.
Relic and archeotech effects do not stack with another copy of the same named item. Relic weapons and armour are 
already exceptional objects and cannot receive additional weapon or armour modifications unless their entry explicitly 
allows it. Masterwork Traits may be part of a relic profile, but are not added automatically.
Burden is part of the item. A Burden can represent maintenance, legal ownership, factional obligation, dangerous 
provenance, rare ammunition or unwanted attention. The GM should use a Burden to create decisions and 
consequences, not to remove a hard-won reward without warning.

Archeotech represents technology whose manufacture is poorly understood, lost or institutionally restricted. Its 
Availability describes access, not the ability to mass-produce it.
Item Availability Effect
Volkite Serpenta Exceptional 1d10 radiant/fire; 50/150 ft; Light, Reload 8. Once per turn when you hit a 
Bloodied target, deal +1d6 fire damage.
Volkite Charger Near-Unique 2d8 radiant/fire; 80/240 ft; Burst, Reload 12. Once per turn, if the target has 
already taken damage this round, deal +1d8 fire damage.
Suspensor Harness Exceptional
Choose one Heavy weapon you carry. You ignore its movement-based 
Heavy penalty. If it is Emplaced, you may fire it as though it were merely 
Heavy while the harness is functioning. Requires Strength 13+ or an 
appropriate interface.
Archeotech Logic Engine Exceptional
Advantage on Technology checks to identify or operate ancient machinery. 
Once per short rest, after rolling an Intelligence or Technology check, add 
1d8 before the result is declared.
Phase-Shunt Field Near-Unique
Once per long rest when damage would reduce you to 0 HP but not kill you 
outright, remain at 1 HP and teleport up to 15 ft to a visible unoccupied 
space. The field becomes Damaged after use until properly repaired.
Medicae Crucible Exceptional
Once per long rest as an action, a creature you touch regains 4d8 + 
proficiency bonus HP and ends Poisoned or one disease. It may suppress 
one lasting-injury penalty until its next long rest, but does not cure the 
injury.

Faction relics are named or storied objects. Their provenance matters as much as their rules: carrying one can create 
authority, suspicion, obligations or enemies.
Relic Availability Effect
The Last Light - Imperial Near-Unique
Lasgun: 1d10 radiant; 100/300 ft; Accurate, Armour-Breaking, Reload 30. 
Once per short rest on a hit, choose a second creature directly behind the 
target within 30 ft; if the original attack roll would hit it, it takes 1d10 radiant 
damage.
Bulwark of Saint Drusus - Imperial Near-Unique
Refractor relic. Once per short rest, reaction to reduce damage to you by 
2d8 + proficiency bonus; allies within 5 ft reduce the same instance of area 
damage by your proficiency bonus. Burden: Ecclesiarchal or Inquisitorial 
ownership is likely.
Martyr's Censer - Imperial Exceptional
Once per long rest as an action, for 1 minute, allies within 15 ft have 
advantage on fear and Corruption saves. Daemons and explicitly corrupted 
creatures that start their turn in the aura take radiant damage equal to your 
proficiency bonus.
Arc of the Reductor - Mechanicus Near-Unique
Arc rifle: 2d8 lightning; 80/240 ft; Shock, Armour-Breaking, Mechanicus, 
Reload 8. Once per short rest, a hit against a machine, vehicle or structure 
becomes a critical hit.
Omnissian Data-Relic - 
Mechanicus Near-Unique
While interfaced, gain +1 to Technology checks and advantage to identify 
Mechanicus systems. Once per short rest, reroll a failed Technology check. 
Burden: the Cult Mechanicus regards the device as institutional property.
Big Lug's Door - Ogryn Near-Unique
+2 AC; Ogryn only; counts as a Slab Shield. If you did not move this turn, 
one Small or Medium ally directly behind you has Full Cover. Once per 
short rest when a ranged attack misses you, move 5 ft toward the attacker 
without provoking opportunity attacks.
Relic Availability Effect
Grutt's Lucky Club - Ogryn Exceptional
2d6 bludgeoning; Melee; Ogryn, Heavy, Brutal. Once per short rest when 
you miss with it, reroll the attack. If the reroll hits a Large or smaller target, it 
must pass a Strength save or be pushed 10 ft.
Ancestor-Wrought Rail Rifle - Kin Near-Unique
2d10 force; 150/450 ft; Accurate, Heavy, Armour-Breaking, Reload 2. Once 
per short rest, one attack ignores Light and Heavy Cover and one source of 
resistance to its weapon damage.
Oathplate of the First Claim - Kin Near-Unique
AC 17, max Dex +1; Kin only; no Speed penalty. Once per short rest, 
ignore one effect that would shove, knock you prone, or reduce your Speed. 
Allies within 5 ft gain +1 to saves against forced movement while you are 
conscious.
Ghosthelm of the Wandering Seer 
- Aeldari Near-Unique
Aeldari Warlock or GM-approved Psyker. Once per long rest when Perils 
trigger, treat the severity result as Warp Static. After resolving it, reduce 
your Warp Pressure by your proficiency bonus, minimum 0.
Starfall Long Rifle - Aeldari Near-Unique
1d10 piercing; 180/720 ft; Accurate, Silent, Monomolecular, Reload 6. If you 
are Hidden and did not move this turn, attacks with it score a critical hit on 
19-20. Once per short rest, ignore Heavy Cover on one attack.

Unique items have no ordinary Requisition test. Each should be tied to a mission, inheritance, patron, theft, recovered 
vault, political bargain or equivalent campaign event. The examples below are templates for campaign-defining rewards 
rather than assumptions about what every high-level character owns.
Unique Item Availability Effect and Burden
Halo of Saint Varro Unique
Once per long rest as a bonus action, for 1 minute, you and allies within 15 
ft have advantage on fear and Corruption saves; you gain resistance to 
psychic and force damage. Burden: visible possession attracts 
Ecclesiarchal attention and expectations.
Heart-Key of the Red Vault Unique
Mechanicus interface. Once per long rest, treat one Technology check to 
unlock, disable or command a machine, security system or vehicle of DC 20 
or lower as a success. Against harder systems, make the check with 
advantage and add 1d10. Burden: multiple forge worlds claim it.
The First Oathstone Unique
Kin relic. Once per long rest, when a creature harms you or an ally within 30 
ft, name it oath-bound for 1 minute. Once each round when an ally hits that 
creature, that ally adds your proficiency bonus to the damage. Burden: 
abandoning the oath has serious cultural consequences.
The Veiled Eye Unique
Aeldari spirit-lens. Once per long rest as a bonus action, for 1 minute, you 
can see Invisible and Hidden creatures within 60 ft, cannot be Surprised, 
and your ranged attacks ignore Light Cover. Burden: The item carries a 
psychic echo noticeable to Aeldari and Warp-sensitive beings.
The Door That Would Not Break Unique
+2 AC; Ogryn only; counts as a Slab Shield and has no Speed penalty. If 
you do not move, up to two Small or Medium allies directly behind you have 
Full Cover. Once per long rest, when a weapon attack hits you, reduce that 
attack's damage to 0. Burden: it is enormous and impossible to conceal.
The Ghost's Coin Unique
Black-market data-sigil. Once per long rest, produce a convincing identity, 
access token or ownership record appropriate to the current settlement or 
institution; for one scene, gain advantage on Deception and Investigation 
checks that rely on it. Burden: every use risks attracting whoever originally 
issued the stolen credentials.

When the GM creates another relic, start with an existing weapon, armour or item rather than inventing a new 
numerical scale. Add one memorable capability, one limited high-impact ability, or one rule-changing interaction. If an 
item simply grants a permanent +1 attack, +1 AC or a reroll, use the Master-Crafted rules instead. Relics should create 
choices, tactics or story consequences rather than mandatory arithmetic upgrades.

succeeds.

manualRules.text:
Availability answers how difficult an item is to obtain. Provenance answers who made it, who claims it, who can 
maintain it and what happens if you are caught carrying it. A successful Requisition test never erases provenance.
Provenance Normal Access Typical Complication
Imperial General Militarum, Arbites, Inquisition, sanctioned 
institutions and ordinary Imperial markets.
Rank, paperwork, mission need, local 
shortages or questions about ownership.
Mechanicus Forge worlds, tech-priests, Skitarii supply 
and approved workshops.
Ritual restrictions, machine-cult authority, 
data access or maintenance dependency.
Kin Kin holds, guilds, prospectors and trusted 
trade contacts.
Cultural ownership, ammunition 
compatibility and reluctance to arm 
outsiders.
Provenance Normal Access Typical Complication
Aeldari Craftworld, ranger, corsair or outcast 
networks.
Imperial illegality, alien maintenance, 
hidden obligations and suspicion from both 
sides.
Proscribed / Heretical No routine lawful source.
Confiscation, corruption, Heat, 
investigation, spiritual danger or outright 
execution if exposed.
Black Market Brokers, smugglers, gangers, scavengers 
and corrupt officials.
Fraud, debt, damaged goods, traceable 
serials, betrayal or the wrong provenance.
Faction access is contextual rather than a second currency. A character normally treats equipment from their own 
institution or culture as plausible at its listed Availability. Gear from another provenance may require a contact, narrative 
permission, a +2 to +5 DC increase, or a different acquisition route altogether. Aeldari and Kin player characters do not 
automatically make their equipment legal inside the Imperium; they merely provide a believable route to obtaining and 
maintaining it.

Tier does not hard-lock equipment. It describes what the campaign can usually support without exceptional story 
justification. A low-level character can carry a relic if the story gives them one; a high-level character can still be stuck 
with a battered lasgun after capture or disaster.
Tier Levels Normal Access Typical Exceptional Reward
Tier 1 1-4 Issued and Controlled gear. Scarce items appear 
as specialist mission assets.
One Scarce item, unusual modification, or limited-
use specialist ammunition.
Tier 2 5-10 Issued, Controlled and Scarce gear. Rare items 
become plausible rewards or difficult requisitions.
A Rare weapon, advanced augmetic, field or power 
weapon, or first master-crafted item.
Tier 3 11-16
Scarce gear is routine for established warbands; 
Rare equipment is attainable through strong faction 
access.
Exceptional armoury access, advanced master-
crafted gear, archeotech fragments or major 
faction-specific wargear.
Tier 4 17-20
Rare equipment can be expected around elite 
operatives. Exceptional gear remains politically and 
narratively important.
Exceptional or Near-Unique relic access tied to 
major obligations, patrons or campaign events.

Most non-relic weapons have one modification slot. A master-crafted weapon may have two. A weapon cannot take the 
same modification twice, and a modification must make physical and fictional sense for the weapon. The GM may 
rename an upgrade to match its culture or technology without changing the rule.
Modification Availability Effect
Bayonet / Breaching Lug Issued
A suitable ranged weapon can be used as a 1d6 piercing melee weapon 
without drawing another weapon. It is not Finesse unless the base weapon 
is Light.
Extended Magazine / Charge Pack Controlled Increase the weapon's Reload value by 25%, rounded up. Does not apply 
to Reload 1 weapons or single-use launchers.
Reflex Sight Controlled Once per short rest, after you roll a ranged attack but before the result is 
declared, add +1d4 to the roll.
Camo Wrap / Low-Signature 
Furniture Controlled Advantage on one check per short rest to conceal, hide or disguise the 
weapon.
Recoil Compensation Scarce Once per short rest, ignore disadvantage or another penalty caused 
specifically by moving before firing a Heavy weapon.
Targeting Optic Scarce When you Aim and do not move before the attack, ignore Light Cover on 
one ranged attack.
Reinforced Action Scarce
The first time each mission the weapon would become Damaged because

manualRules.text:
Master-crafted gear is not an ordinary shopping upgrade. It is normally Rare or Exceptional, comes from a named 
maker or institution, and should matter enough that losing it hurts. A master-crafted item has one Masterwork Trait. 
Particularly important relic-grade items may have a second trait at the GM's discretion. Bonuses from duplicate 
Masterwork Traits never stack.
Masterwork Trait Eligible Item Effect
Perfect Balance Melee or ranged weapon Gain +1 to attack rolls made with the item.
Artificer Edge Melee weapon Once per turn when you roll weapon damage, reroll one damage die and 
use the new result.
Precision Barrel / Focusing 
Array Ranged weapon Increase normal range by 25%. This does not increase maximum range 
beyond double the new normal range.
Rapid Feed Reload weapon Increase Reload by 50%, rounded up. Does not stack with Extended 
Magazine.
Masterwork Trait Eligible Item Effect
Recoil Compensation Heavy ranged weapon Moving before firing no longer imposes a penalty from the Heavy 
property, though other Heavy restrictions still apply.
Compact Pattern Pistol, basic firearm or 
compact melee weapon
Advantage on checks to conceal the item; it can be readied from 
concealment without an item interaction once per turn.
Artificer Armour Armour Increase the armour's AC by +1. A shield or field cannot gain this trait.
Responsive Plating Armour Once per short rest, reduce damage from one non-critical weapon hit by 
your proficiency bonus.
Sealed Systems Armour
Gain advantage on saves against gas, smoke and airborne toxins. If the 
armour is already sealed, it also tolerates brief vacuum exposure without 
a separate suit breach test.
Bounded accuracy matters. The +1 attack or +1 AC traits above are intentionally powerful and should remain 
uncommon. They represent prized equipment, not a mandatory mathematical treadmill.

manualRules.text:
Read a profile: AC protects the hull; HP measures structural damage; DT is its Damage Threshold (21.5); Speed is 
tactical movement in feet per round. Handling modifies driving checks and vehicle Dexterity saves. Crew lists working 
stations; Passengers lists additional seats. Cargo is capacity after the listed occupants and their normal gear.
Vehicles proficiency adds your proficiency bonus to Dexterity (Vehicles) checks and can qualify you for mounted-
weapon attacks. Add proficiency only once, even if another proficiency applies. Anyone may attempt ordinary driving. 
Unfamiliar alien controls require instruction or a compatible interface before use. Technology repairs vehicles; it does 
not replace Vehicles for driving.
Stations: D = driver, G = gunner, L = loader. One conscious driver at the controls is required to move. Other stations 
may remain empty but cannot act. A G operates one weapon at a time; an L may reload a mount. A one-crew vehicle 
lets its driver operate its listed weapon. A passenger must enter a crew station before using it.
Turns: each character keeps their own initiative, action, bonus action and reaction. The vehicle grants no extra turns. 
On their turn, a driver may spend their entire personal movement allowance to move the vehicle up to its Speed, 
without spending an action. The vehicle receives this movement only once per round, even if drivers swap. Riding does 
not spend a passenger’s movement.
Station changes: boarding a stationary vehicle, disembarking or changing to an accessible station costs 10 ft of 
personal movement. A driver who spent their movement cannot then disembark normally that turn. Small and Medium 
creatures use one seat. An Ogryn uses three passenger spaces and needs suitable access and reinforcement. 
Ordinary crew stations require the Ogryn accommodation upgrade; bikes and undersized chassis cannot take it.

All these mounts count as Heavy and Emplaced, resolved using 21.3. The heavy stubber, heavy bolter and multi-laser 
retain Chapter 8 damage, range and other properties. Range is in feet; two numbers mean normal/maximum range. A 
single area range is the furthest point the gunner may choose.
Weapon Damage Range Properties Availability
Heavy stubber 1d12 piercing 120/360 Burst, Suppression; Reload 40 Controlled
Heavy bolter 1d12 piercing + 1d6 
thunder 100/300 Burst, Brutal, Suppression; Reload 30 Scarce
Multi-laser 2d8 radiant 120/360 Burst; Reload 40 Scarce
Autocannon 2d10 piercing 160/480 Armour-Breaking; Reload 10 Rare
Lascannon 4d10 radiant 200/600 Armour-Breaking; Reload 5 Rare
Battle cannon 3d10 piercing + 3d10 
thunder 240 15-ft radius; Armour-Breaking; Reload 1 Exceptional
Bolt cannon 3d8 piercing 120/360 Burst, Brutal; Reload 12 Rare
HYLas rotary cannon 3d8 radiant 120/360 Burst; Reload 20 Rare
Magna-coil autocannon 3d10 piercing 160/480 Armour-Breaking; Reload 8 Rare
Scatter laser 3d8 radiant 160/480 Burst; Reload 24 Rare
Shuriken cannon 2d10 slashing 120/360 Burst, Monomolecular; Reload 18 Rare
Twin shuriken catapults 1d8 slashing 60/180 Burst, Monomolecular, Twin-Linked; 
Reload 24 Scarce
Pulse laser 4d10 radiant 200/600 Armour-Breaking; Reload 6 Exceptional
Battle cannon: choose a visible point within 240 ft. Creatures and vehicles within 15 ft make Dexterity saves against 
the gunner’s mounted save DC, taking full damage on failure or half on success. Full Cover blocks the blast. Apply 
Armour-Breaking and DT after the save. No attack roll, critical hit or Dexterity damage modifier applies. Spend one 
shell; reloading loads one from the eight-shell mission supply.
Burst uses the Chapter 7 −2 attack penalty and extra damage die. It expends three shots instead of one and 
requires at least three remaining. For mixed dice, an extra Burst or Brutal die is the first damage die listed. 
Area weapons cannot use Burst. A Suppression mount may require one creature it hits to make a Wisdom save 
against the mounted save DC; failure applies Suppressed as in 6.3. Hulls are immune.
Reload X is the current magazine’s remaining firing uses; Burst consumes three. An action by the gunner or loader fills 
it to X from compatible stores. Ordinary spare magazines are abstracted unless scarcity was declared; battle cannon 
shells are always counted. This list does not grant additional mounts.
Loadout options: with GM approval, replace a Sentinel multi-laser with a lascannon or a Vyper scatter laser with a 
shuriken cannon. Retain stations and firing limits. A pulse laser needs a suitable heavy Aeldari chassis and is not a 
normal Vyper upgrade.
Damage example: a heavy bolter hits a Chimera (DT 10) for 8 piercing + 5 thunder. The combined 13 meets DT, so 
apply all 13 HP damage. A separate 9-damage hit does nothing. Armour-Breaking instead compares damage with DT 
5. Passengers are not automatically damaged.

manualRules.text:
Clear roads and ordinary turns need no roll. Follow a physically possible route: a vehicle cannot pass through walls or 
gaps narrower than its hull. Reversing costs double movement. Walkers turn in place; other vehicles need room to turn. 
Rubble, stairs and steep slopes are difficult terrain unless a trait says otherwise. Tactical Speed is not maximum road 
speed. For map space, use 10 × 10 ft for Large, 15 × 15 ft for Huge, and at least 20 × 20 ft for Gargantuan; the GM can 
use the actual hull outline when terrain demands it.
Difficulty Example DC
Routine Clear road, ordinary turn, controlled stop None
Demanding Sharp turn, loose surface, narrow opening 10
Dangerous Dense wreckage, unstable bridge, hard evasive turn 13
Extreme Broken causeway jump or collapsing route 16
Exceptional A barely possible stunt under severe pressure 20
Roll Dexterity (Vehicles) + Handling. Failure ends movement before the hazard; failure by 5 or more also causes a 
collision (21.4). The GM may state a different consequence before the roll. A natural 1 is not an automatic crash; a 
natural 20 cannot make an impossible stunt possible.
A skimmer operates within 10 ft of a supporting surface. It can cross terrain or calm water allowed by its profile but 
cannot climb above a wall to bypass a scene. When its drive fails, it settles onto the surface below; a fall into a chasm 
remains a fall. Falls deal 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 ft, maximum 20d6, ignoring DT; exposed occupants take their own 
falling damage, while enclosed occupants use the wreck rules if the hull reaches 0 HP.
Vehicle Combat

manualRules.text:
Action Effect
Drive Hard
Driver: move up to the vehicle’s Speed again. Once per vehicle per round. Until the driver’s next 
turn, attacks from it have disadvantage and targets have advantage on saves against its mounted 
area weapons.
Evasive Driving
Driver: declare before vehicle movement; cap that movement at half Speed. Until the driver’s next 
turn, attacks against the hull have disadvantage and it has advantage on Dexterity saves. Attacks 
from it have disadvantage; targets have advantage on saves against its mounted area weapons. 
Cannot combine with Drive Hard.
Fire a Mount At its station, make one mounted attack or use one mounted area weapon. Extra Attack does not 
add shots. Each mount can fire only once per round, including reactions.
Reload a Mount At its station or loader position, reload one mount. Each mount can be reloaded only once per 
round.
Spot or Assist Use Help to give one ally advantage on their next driving check or mounted attack before your next 
turn. A useful view, communication and plausible assistance are required.
Damage Control At the affected system: action and DC 13 Intelligence (Technology) check to clear one weapon 
jam, engine stall or vehicle fire. Restores no HP.
One action cannot both drive and fire. A one-crew vehicle can move normally and fire using its driver’s action, but 
cannot Drive Hard and fire that turn. Readying a mount uses Ready and a reaction; its once-per-round limit still applies. 
An explicitly granted additional action may fire a different mount that the operator can access.
Mounted attack = d20 + Dexterity modifier + proficiency if proficient in Vehicles or that weapon. Add Dexterity to 
damage once on a hit. Mounted save DC = 8 + Dexterity modifier + proficiency if trained. Area weapons add no ability 
modifier to damage. A mount removes normal Heavy and Emplaced movement restrictions; other properties still apply. 
Personal-weapon-only features do not automatically apply to mounts.
Turret mounts fire in any direction; forward mounts fire in a 90-degree arc centred on the hull’s front. Terrain and the 
hull still block line of fire. Vehicle movement counts as occupant movement for Accurate and other “did not move” 
benefits. Personal weapons retain their normal rules, including Extra Attack; they do not use Fire a Mount.
Closed compartments provide Full Cover from outside attacks and effects that cannot pass through the hull. Open-
topped vehicles and exposed riders provide Light Cover where the hull blocks the line of fire. Using a hatch or firing 
port exposes that occupant with Heavy Cover until their next turn. One occupant uses each firing port per round. Target 
a visible occupant using their own AC. Hull hits do not also hit the crew.
Area effects resolve separately against the hull and exposed occupants in the area. Full Cover protects enclosed 
occupants unless an effect penetrates it. Vehicle Strength saves use +2 for Large, +4 for Huge or +6 for Gargantuan; 
Constitution saves use +4. Dexterity saves use the driver’s Dexterity (Vehicles) modifier + Handling. An uncontrolled or 
immobilised vehicle automatically fails Dexterity saves.

Ram: the driver spends an action, moves at least 20 ft straight using available vehicle movement, and chooses a target 
in the path. It makes a Dexterity save against 8 + the driver’s Dexterity modifier + Vehicles proficiency, if trained. 
Damage is 4d6 bludgeoning for a Large rammer, 6d6 for Huge or 8d6 for Gargantuan. A creature takes half on a 
successful save and moves to the nearest safe space. A vehicle that succeeds avoids the ram if it has a clear path; 
otherwise it fails. Fixed obstacles automatically fail.
On contact the rammer stops. A struck vehicle or solid obstacle deals half the rolled damage back to it. An accidental 
collision deals the full size-based damage to the moving vehicle and obstacle. Apply DT normally. A vehicle can ram 
once per round and cannot also Drive Hard. Hull damage harms occupants only if it causes a wreck.

manualRules.text:
Damage Threshold: total all damage from one hit or effect after resistance, then compare it with DT. Below DT, the 
hull takes no damage. At least DT, apply the full total. DT is a threshold, not damage reduction. Do not combine 
separate attacks to overcome it.
Against a hull, Armour-Breaking also halves DT for that hit, rounded down. It does not reduce AC or bypass Full Cover. 
This extends the Chapter 7 property. Power Field and Monomolecular do not bypass DT unless explicitly stated. 
Personal weapons can harm hulls when they overcome DT.
Vehicles are objects. Hulls are immune to poison, disease, radiation, fear, Suppression and effects that target only 
creatures or minds. Psychic damage cannot harm a hull unless the power explicitly affects machinery or objects. 
Vehicles do not make death saves, recover through rests or benefit from creature-only healing. Drivers and exposed 
occupants suffer conditions normally; their personal resistances do not protect the hull.
Roll one breakdown when a critical hit damages the hull, or when it first reaches half maximum HP or less in an 
encounter. If it begins at half HP or less, roll on its first damaging hit instead. Maximum one breakdown roll per vehicle 
per round; simultaneous triggers give one roll. Critical hits otherwise double damage dice normally.
d6 Breakdown Effect
1 Running gear Speed is halved until repaired; minimum 5 ft unless already 0.
2 Steering Disadvantage on driving checks and vehicle Dexterity saves until repaired.
3 Weapon jam One random fitted mount cannot fire until Damage Control succeeds. With no mount, 
use result 2.
4 Hull breach Lose Sealed. One random enclosed occupant position provides only Heavy Cover until 
repaired.
5 Engine stall Speed becomes 0 and remaining movement is lost until Damage Control succeeds.
6 Vehicle fire At the end of the driver’s turn, hull takes 2d6 fire damage ignoring DT. If uncontrolled, 
use the former driver’s initiative. Damage Control extinguishes it.
Breakdowns do not stack with themselves. A repeated active result instead deals 2d6 hull damage ignoring DT; this 
cannot trigger another breakdown. Field or workshop repair clears running-gear, steering or hull-breach damage (21.8). 
Damage Control clears only jams, stalls and fires.
At 0 HP the vehicle is Wrecked: stop movement and disable its mounts. Each occupant makes a DC 13 Dexterity 
save, taking 2d6 bludgeoning on failure or half on success. Conscious occupants may immediately leave into an 
unoccupied space within 5 ft without an action. Anyone remaining must later leave normally or be rescued. Wrecks do 
not automatically explode. Fire or hazardous cargo may create a separately signalled danger.
Uncontrolled movement: when a vehicle would next move without a conscious driver, it coasts straight up to 30 ft, 
limited by the distance it moved last round, then stops. Resolve obstacles as collisions. A new driver at the controls 
before then can prevent the coast. Swapping drivers never grants a second movement allowance in the round.

Boarding in motion: from within 5 ft, spend an action and make DC 13 Athletics or Acrobatics to reach an exposed 
foothold. DC 16 if either vehicle used Drive Hard this round. Failure leaves you where you started; failure by 5 or more 
also puts you Prone in the nearest safe space and deals 2d6 bludgeoning. Closed or locked hatches must still be 
opened or breached. Moving inside then costs normal movement.
Jumping out of a moving vehicle uses the same action, check and failure damage. No check is needed if it has not 
moved since the start of its driver’s last turn. A passing hull may be targeted by an opportunity melee attack as if it were 
a creature; carried occupants do not provoke just because the vehicle moves. Normal creature-only grapples and 
shoves cannot move a vehicle.

manualRules.text:
Use chase bands when routes and obstacles matter more than squares. Choose pursuer and quarry, then set a 
starting band. Bands replace tactical movement between those vehicles: do not also add Speed or Drive Hard to the 
gap. Actions and damage still use normal rounds.
Band Separation Range
0 — Contact Alongside or immediately behind 10 ft
1 — Close A short stretch of road 60 ft
2 — Near A clear firing lane 120 ft
3 — Far Terrain or traffic intervenes 240 ft
4 — Distant Almost lost from sight 480 ft
5 — Lost Beyond immediate pursuit Out of sight
At round’s end, each driver who spent their action Pursuing rolls Dexterity (Vehicles) + Handling. The vehicle with the 
faster current Speed grants +2 in that contest; equal Speed grants neither side a bonus. A quarry win increases the 
gap one band; a pursuer win decreases it one. A margin of 5 or more changes it two bands. Ties leave it unchanged. 
Clamp gaps between 0 and 5.
Pursuing uses the driver’s action instead of firing, ramming, Drive Hard or Evasive Driving. If only one driver Pursues, 
that driver wins by one band without a contest; if neither does, the gap stays unchanged. A stopped quarry is caught; a 
stopped pursuer loses. At band 5 the quarry escapes after staying there through the next contest; the pursuer can still 
close on that contest but cannot attack an unseen target.
The GM may introduce one route hazard per vehicle per round, with a DC 10, 13 or 16 driving check. Failure gives 
disadvantage on that round’s chase contest; failure by 5 also causes a collision. Announce consequences first. A 
navigator may Help with either a hazard or contest, not both. Other crew can attack, reload or repair using the band’s 
range. There is no extra firing penalty just for Pursuing.
At Contact, use an action to ram or board instead of another action. With several vehicles, roll once per driver and 
reuse the base roll in each contest, applying the faster-vehicle +2 separately. Example: a Taurox pursues a hauler at 
Near. Final totals of 18 and 14 favour the Taurox by 4, closing to Close. An attack earlier that round still used Near’s 
120-ft distance.

manualRules.text:
Use Chapter 18’s Availability and provenance rules. Success normally grants a mission loan or support, not personal 
ownership. Agree the chassis, listed weapons, supplies, crew arrangements, route and recovery conditions. Vehicles 
are not class starting equipment unless explicitly granted by the GM.
Civilian transport fits early missions; armed scouts and carriers require credible faction support. Tanks and alien grav-
tanks are substantial assets, even for experienced warbands. Low-level crews can be assigned one, but need a reason 
it cannot solve every obstacle. Captured vehicles still require access, supplies, maintenance and a safe destination; 
possessing one does not make its use lawful or consequence-free.
Each vehicle has two modification slots. Fit one upgrade per slot and never duplicate it. Fitting or replacing one takes 
four hours in a suitable workshop with tools. Undamaged upgrades can be recovered. Built-in traits use no slots. 
Personal armour or weapon upgrades do not apply to hulls or mounts unless explicitly permitted.
Upgrade Availability Effect
Reinforced plating Rare
Add 20 maximum and current HP when fitted. Speed −10 ft, minimum 
10 ft. Removal removes 20 current HP, minimum 1. No AC or DT 
increase.
Smoke launchers Controlled
Two uses per mission. Driver or gunner action creates stationary smoke in a 
20-ft radius centred on the vehicle until the start of that operator’s next turn. 
Attacks through it have disadvantage; no protection against area effects.
Auspex survey suite Scarce
A crew member scanning as an action gains advantage on one Perception or 
Survival check for routes, obstacles or ambushes within 300 ft. Does not see 
through solid barriers.
Recovery winch Controlled
At rest, an operator’s action pulls an unsecured or willing object up to cargo 
capacity by 10 ft. With a sound anchor, ten minutes frees the vehicle from 
ordinary mud or a shallow ditch.
All-terrain running gear Scarce Wheeled or tracked chassis ignores difficult terrain from mud, loose rubble 
and shallow debris; not walls, deep water or impassable slopes.
Sealed compartment Rare Enclosed chassis gains Sealed and one hour of internal air. Cannot fit to 
exposed bikes or open-topped vehicles.
Ogryn accommodation Controlled
Convert one suitable crew station for an Ogryn OR reinforce suitable 
passenger space so an Ogryn uses two spaces instead of three. Choose one 
version; no duplicates. Chassis must have enough physical room.
Spare-parts locker Scarce
Includes two repair kits. Once per mission reroll one failed field-repair check, 
using the new result. Expended kits need replacement; locker remains 
reusable.
Weapon swaps need GM approval, the new weapon’s Availability, a compatible mount and four workshop hours. A 
swap replaces a mount’s weapon; it does not add a weapon or crew station. An integral bike or walker weapon cannot 
be removed and wielded as an ordinary personal firearm.
Travel times follow the route and the vehicle’s fictional capabilities, not a conversion of tactical Speed into miles per 
hour. A compact chase, a breakdown and a choice of route are usually more useful than tracking fuel for every mile.
Vehicle Profiles

Squats, also called Kin in many modern Imperial records, 
are not simply short humans. They are dense,
hardy, void-adapted, stubborn, and culturally bound to 
clan, hold, oath, guild, and ancestor-core
traditions.
Squats/Kin may be Kin Armsmen or Hernkyn 
Prospectors. They cannot be Psykers, Zealots, Arbites,
Skitarii, Ogryns, Ratling Sharpshooters, or Aeldari 
classes.
A Squat/Kin character in an Imperial warband should 
have a clear reason for cooperation: a trade
contract, mercenary oath, salvage claim, ancient grudge, 
debt, diplomatic mission, or shared enemy.

When a task has an uncertain outcome, roll d20 + the 
relevant ability modifier. If you are proficient in the skill or 
tool that applies, also add your proficiency bonus. A 
saving throw uses the same structure, adding proficiency 
only when your class or another rule grants proficiency in 
that saving throw.
Advantage and disadvantage: roll two d20s and use the 
higher result for advantage or the lower result for 
disadvantage. Multiple sources of the same type do not 
stack; if you have both advantage and disadvantage, 
they cancel, and you roll one d20.

manualRules.text:
If you can make more than one attack with the Attack action, a grapple or shove may replace one of those attacks. You 
must have at least one free hand to grapple a creature.
Maneuver Procedure
Grapple
Choose a creature within your reach that is no more than one size larger than you. Make a 
Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). 
On a success, the target is grappled.
Escape
A grappled creature may use its action to repeat the contest. On a success, the grapple ends. 
The grapple also ends if the grappler is incapacitated or the creatures are moved beyond the 
grappler's reach.
Move a Grappled Target When you move, you may drag or carry a grappled target, but your Speed is halved unless the 
target is at least two sizes smaller than you.
Shove Choose a creature within your reach that is no more than one size larger than you. Make the 
same contested check as a grapple. On a success, either push the target 5 ft or knock it Prone.

make one attack with a different one-handed Light melee weapon in your other hand. Do not add your ability modifier to

weapons follows the normal item-interaction limits unless a feature says otherwise.

feature that grants a bonus-action pistol attack, such as a Gunslinger or Talent feature, may use either ready pistol. 
Reload each firearm separately. Carrying a pistol and a blade likewise grants no extra attack unless a feature provides 
one.

Rest Duration Effect
Short Rest At least 1 hour
A period of relative safety with no strenuous activity. You may spend Hit Dice; for each 
die spent, roll it and regain HP equal to the result + your Constitution modifier. Recover 
features that say they return on a short rest. Warp Pressure is reduced to 0 as described 
in Chapter 15.
Long Rest At least 8 hours
At least 6 hours should be sleep or an equivalent species-appropriate rest unless the 
GM rules otherwise. Restore all lost HP, recover long-rest features and regain spent Hit 
Dice up to half your total Hit Dice, minimum one. Warp Pressure is reduced to 0. A 
character can normally benefit from only one long rest in 24 hours.
Rest does not remove Corruption, lasting injuries, lost equipment or narrative consequences unless a specific rule says 
otherwise.

The following definitions apply when a rule gives a creature one of these conditions or states. If a feature gives a more 
specific duration or effect, the specific feature wins.
Condition / State Effect
Blinded You cannot see and automatically fail checks that require sight. Your attacks have disadvantage; 
attacks against you have advantage.
Bloodied You are Bloodied while at or below half your maximum HP. Bloodied is a state, not a condition, 
and has no effect by itself unless a rule refers to it.
Charmed You cannot attack or deliberately harm the creature that charmed you. That creature has 
advantage on social checks made against you.
Frightened
While you can see the source of your fear, you have disadvantage on ability checks and attack 
rolls and cannot willingly move closer to it. A "fear save" is a save made to avoid or end this 
condition.
Grappled Your Speed becomes 0 and cannot benefit from bonuses to Speed. The condition ends if the 
grappler is incapacitated or you are moved beyond its reach.
Hidden
You are unseen and unheard by a creature that has not located you. Attacks against a creature 
you are hidden from normally have advantage. Making an attack normally reveals your position 
after the attack resolves unless a feature says otherwise.
Incapacitated You cannot take actions, bonus actions or reactions.
Invisible
You cannot be seen without a special sense or effect. Your attacks normally have advantage, 
and attacks against you normally have disadvantage. You can still be detected by sound, tracks 
or other evidence.
Poisoned You have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

says scarcity matters. Ammo Packs in Chapter 17 are 
used when ammunition is limited, an emergency resupply 
is needed, or specialist ammunition must be restored.

States from the GM Guide.

di.species.aeldari.descriptionMarkdown:
3.6 Aeldari / Eldar
Aeldari are ancient xenos whose reflexes, senses, and 
psychic presence far exceed human norms. Player
Aeldari should represent rare outcasts, rangers, corsair-
adjacent wanderers, or warlocks operating
under a specific hidden purpose.
Ability Scores: +2 Dexterity, +1 Intelligence or Wisdom.
Size: Medium.
Speed: 35 ft.
Available Classes: Aeldari Outcast, Aeldari Warlock.
3.6.1 Aeldari Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 90 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Inhuman Grace: Gain proficiency in Acrobatics or 
Stealth.
Keen Senses: Gain proficiency in Perception. If you 
already have Perception proficiency, add +1 to
Perception checks instead.
Battle Trance: You may move through the space of 
allied creatures without treating it as difficult
terrain. Once per short rest, when you move at least 10 ft 
before making a weapon attack, add +1d4 to
the attack roll.
Ancient Mind: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being charmed or frightened by non-psychic 
effects.
Xenos Distrust: You have disadvantage on Persuasion 
checks with most Imperial authorities unless
disguised, vouched for, or operating under an established 
truce.

di.species.kin.descriptionMarkdown:
3.5 Squat / Kin
Squats, often known as Kin in modern Imperial records, 
are hardy void-adapted abhumans associated
with holds, guilds, oath-bands, mining fleets, mercenary 
contracts, and ancient grudges. They are
shorter than humans but dense, resilient, technically 
minded, and extremely difficult to intimidate.
Ability Scores: +2 Constitution, +1 Intelligence or 
Wisdom.
Size: Medium, but your height is usually between 4 and 5 
ft.
Speed: 25 ft.
Available Classes: Kin Armsman, Hernkyn Prospector.
3.5.1 Squat / Kin Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 60 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Dense Build: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being shoved, knocked prone, or moved
against your will.
Void-Hardened: You have advantage on saving throws 
against exhaustion caused by poor atmosphere,
bad rations, forced marches, cramped voidship 
conditions, mining hazards, or environmental hardship.
Guild-Craft: Gain proficiency in Technology, 
Investigation, or one artisan/tool proficiency related to
engineering, mining, weapons, armour, or voidcraft.
Grudge Memory: Once per long rest, when a creature 
damages you or an ally within 30 ft, mark that
creature as the subject of a grudge. The first time you hit 
that creature before the end of the encounter,
add your proficiency bonus to the damage.
Stubborn Kin: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.

di.species.ogryn.descriptionMarkdown:
3.2 Ogryn Abhuman
Ogryns are massive abhumans used by the Imperium as 
shock troops, bodyguards, line-breakers, and
living siege weapons. They are loyal and terrifyingly 
durable, but they are not subtle and struggle with
equipment designed for normal human frames.
Ability Scores: +2 Strength, +1 Constitution.
Size: Medium, but you count as one size larger for 
carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, and
shoving.
Speed: 30 ft.
Available Classes: Ogryn Skullbreaker only.
3.2.1 Ogryn Traits
Massive Build: Your maximum hit points increase by 3 
per character level. You also count as one size
larger for carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, 
and shoving.
Thick Skull: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.
Brute Strength: Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 + your 
Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.
Too Big for Standard Kit: You cannot use most 
standard armour, delicate weapons, compact firearms,
or subtle tools unless they have been modified for Ogryn 
use.
Simple Solutions: You are not automatically stupid, but 
you struggle with delicate logic, subtle
interfaces, encrypted systems, and advanced technology. 
You have disadvantage on Intelligence checks
involving advanced technology, forbidden lore, cogitators, 
security systems, encrypted data, or complex
machinery unless you are proficient in a relevant skill or 
tool. However, once per short rest, when a
problem could plausibly be solved through brute force, 
intimidation, endurance, or direct action, you
may add your proficiency bonus to the check even if you 
would not normally be proficient.

proficiency bonus.

availability.message: Human NORMAL Origins: Veteran levels 1–3 and Hive Scum level 1. Ratling NORMAL Hiveborn, Penal, Voidborn, Militarum and Underhive: Veteran or Hive Scum level 1. Twitchy and reviewed kit branches only. Conditional features require manual adjudication.
Rare Origins require trusted GM approval and are unavailable for self-service creation.
Limited Origins require combination-specific campaign approval and are unavailable for self-service creation.
Other species, Ratling higher levels and Sharpshooter remain uncertified. Existing characters retain their pinned profile.
